title: Proposal: Introduce <g> element
body:
This thread is to suggest that `g` element, which stands for "group", be introduced to HTML for optionally grouping elements together. You might think of SVG's `g` element, but this thread talks about HTML.

## Reasons

So why introducing `g` element to HTML? Because:

### It adds more semantics

Many elements are related to each other and can form their own groups, no matter they are block-level or inline-level elements. A well-known example is the child elements of description list `dl`. Take a look at the following code:

```HTML
<dl>
    <dt></dt>
    <dd></dd>
    <dd></dd>
    <dt></dt>
    <dd></dd>
    <dd></dd>
    <dt></dt>
    <dd></dd>
    <dt></dt>
    <dd></dd>
    <dd></dd>
    <dd></dd>
</dl>
```

Very unorganized and hard to read, isn't it? Now take a look at the following code:

```HTML
<dl>
    <g>
        <dt></dt>
        <dd></dd>
        <dd></dd>
    </g>
    <g>
        <dt></dt>
        <dd></dd>
        <dd></dd>
    </g>
    <g>
        <dt></dt>
        <dd></dd>
    </g>
    <g>
        <dt></dt>
        <dd></dd>
        <dd></dd>
        <dd></dd>
    </g>
</dl>
```

The code above is self-explanatory. It is more semantic that related elements be grouped together.

### It helps styling

There have been countless times that we know `dl` element are the perfect candidate for markuping our list contents semantically, but only to realize again that using `dl` element is impractical when it comes to styling because there is no grouping elements inside of it. With the optional `g` element, such headaches will be no more.

### It is optional

`g` element would be meaningful and helpful. But it is not a must. When backward compatibility is necessary, developers can choose to not using it so that legacy browsers would not have rendering issues.

## TL;DR

To sum up, this proposal is to suggest that grouping element `g` be introduced to HTML. It is an optional element. Its purpose is to group elements which are related with each other and not already grouped together.

## Postscript

You might wonder: Why not just use `div` and `span`? The answer is simple: Because `div` and `span` themselves do not have any semantic meaning, and they cannot pass the validation of HTML validator when being used as direct children of `dl` element.
